# PST test fixtures

Small Outlook `.pst` archives used by `../test_pst_parser.py`. They keep the PST
suite self-contained — no personal archive needed to run or debug it — and their
contents are frozen, so `TestBundledFixtures` can assert exact counts, ids,
folder paths and attachment sizes rather than fuzzy quality percentages.

These files are **test data only**. They are not referenced by `main.spec`'s
`datas`, and nothing under `aichat/tests/` is imported from `main.py`, so
PyInstaller does not collect them — they add nothing to the shipped binary.

| File | Size | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `outlook_sample.pst` | 3.2 MB | 23 folders, 11 emails, 34 attachments |
| `aspose_sample.pst` | 265 KB | 8 folders, 1 email, no attachments |

## `outlook_sample.pst`

Written by Outlook, so it carries the full standard folder set. Deliberately
kept because of what it exercises:

- **Nested folders** (`Inbox/SubInbox`) — the client rebuilds its tree by
  splitting these paths.
- **Populated Calendar and Contacts** (one item each) — makes the non-mail
  folder filtering assertions real. An empty Calendar would let a broken filter
  pass.
- **A free/busy system item** in `Freebusy Data`
  (`IPM.Microsoft.ScheduleData.FreeBusy`) — not mail, and not in a folder that
  looks non-mail by name. This is what the `PR_MESSAGE_CLASS` filter is for.
- **Sent Items** — Outlook writes these without transport headers, so sender and
  recipients must come from MAPI properties instead.
- **34 attachments** across PNG/GIF/JPEG/TXT plus embedded `.msg` items, with
  the same filenames repeated in the Inbox and Sent Items copies of a message —
  which is what catches attachment path collisions.
- **HTML bodies** on every message.

All mail is between one test account (`saqib.razzaq@xp.local`, an `xp.local`
lab domain). No real personal data.

## `aspose_sample.pst`

Generated by Aspose.Email for Java (its evaluation watermark is in the message
body). Small and structurally different from anything Outlook writes, which is
the point: it stops the parser from being tuned to Outlook's own layout. It is
also the only fixture with **multiple `To` and `Cc` recipients**, so it pins down
address-list splitting. Addresses are placeholders (`from@domain.com`,
`to1@domain.com`, …).

## Adding or replacing a fixture

`TestBundledFixtures` asserts exact values, so replacing a file means updating
those expectations. Regenerate them with:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python src/aichat/pst_parser.py \
  --file src/aichat/tests/fixtures/<name>.pst --output_dir /tmp/pst-out
```

Several assertions also guard the fixture itself (e.g. "this fixture no longer
contains the free/busy item this test guards") so that a swapped file fails
loudly instead of quietly testing nothing.
